newsitem.title: MEXICO: Marcatel says to offer lower Mexican phone tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Marcatel says to offer lower Mexican phone tariffs.

text.p: Marcatel, the northern Mexican long-distance telephone company, will offer tariffs from two to 15 percent lower than its bigger rivals when the market opens on Jan. 1, a top executive said.
"The price policy of Marcatel is always that we're going to be slightly below the big three, between two and 15 percent lower," said Gustavo M. de la Garza, president of Marcatel.
He was referring to pricing of Telmex, Avantel and Alestra, the three most likely to dominate the market.
Marcatel, product of a union between Radio Beep of Mexico and the U.S. firms IXC Communications and Westel Inc., will try and keep its costs economical to keep tariffs down, de la Garza said.
He said it was initially laying 1,900 kilometers of fiber optic cable, with an investment since August of $1 million a day -- $150 million up to Jan. 10.
By the year 2001, it plans to have invested $650 million.
He said its network will link 29 towns, and will be aimed at small and medium-sized businesses and prosperous homes.
"We are hoping that at the launch we will have two percent of the general market and we expect to have five percent by 1998," he said.
